q: The incompressibility method in combinatorics uses the fact that K(x) ≥ |x| − c for 'most' strings x (incompressible strings). To prove a combinatorial statement about strings of length n, one:
opts: Assumes K(x) = 0 and derives a contradiction
Assumes x is incompressible (K(x) ≥ n − c) and shows that any algorithm compressing x would require K(x) < n − c, reaching a contradiction
Uses the existence of one compressible string
Applies K(x) to the empty string
exp: The incompressibility method: fix a shortest program for x. Since x is incompressible, any description of x (using any structure x might have) has length ≥ n − O(1). This forces the structure to be absent. Used to prove lower bounds in combinatorics and sorting.
